6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision        
6.3 Drivers of two-wheeled vehicles    
6.3.1 Bicycles
To prevent collisions involving cyclists, the following is recommended:
Leave sufficient lateral safety clearance when overtaking, especially if driving a large vehicle (due to the air shocks it can cause), on slopes (since due to the effort and pedalling cyclists can have oscillating trajectories), on windy days (when they can easily be destabilised) or if the cyclist is carrying a passenger.
(Página 256 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Road traffic collisions                      
                       
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision          
6.3 Drivers of two-wheeled vehicles      
6.3.1 Bicycles
To prevent collisions involving cyclists, the following is recommended:
Do not start or continue an overtake if there is a cyclists approaching in the opposite direction.
Exercise extreme caution in bad weather or poor visibility, because there is the increased likelihood of the rider falling or becoming unstable.
Avoid using the warning device (horn) near cyclists. It should only be used when there is sufficient distance to avoid scaring or alarming them.
Be careful when you are parking a vehicle or are near parked cars or other obstacles, as cyclists are able to make sudden movements and change their course quickly.
Exercise caution in housing estates and leisure areas, especially in the summer and school holidays.
(Página 256 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions    
   
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided
With thought and knowledge it is possible to work out where, when, how and why collisions occur and therefore how to avoid them.
Certain circumstances related to the vehicle, the road and the environment but above all the driver, increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision or make the results of a collision much more serious. These circumstances are called “risk factors” and avoiding or minimising them reduces the possibility of being involved in a collision.
Some of these risk factors are fatigue, alcohol, excessive speed, ice or driving with a poorly maintained vehicle, particularly worn tyres.
(Página 249 del manual 'Learning to drive')

2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
All sideways movements, change of direction or ‘U’ turns must be warned of by the following means:
Using the directional indicator (lighting signal) that corresponds to the direction that the vehicle will be turning, or

5 Overtaking
5.1 Concept
Overtaking is the manoeuvre that consists of moving ahead by passing a vehicle or vehicles that travel in front of you at a slower speed.
Note: This also includes passing a vehicle in the same lane as you are travelling in and /or when it doesn’t involve a sideways movement.
(Página 186 del manual 'Learning to drive')

6 Road marks                    
                   
6.2 Longitudinal road markings    
Continuous longitudinal markings
A continuous longitudinal marking means that no driver, whether operating a vehicle or leading an animal, must:
Cross it.
Drive on it.
Drive to the left of the marking when it separates opposing directions of traffic (except in cases provided for in the traffic regulations).
A longitudinal marking formed by two continuous parallel lines has the same meaning as one formed by a single continuous line.
(Página 153 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Maneouvres

questions.question:
Los ocupantes menores de edad de estatura inferior a 135 cm, ¿en qué asientos de un turismo pueden viajar?
In which seats of a passenger car may minors who are under 135 cm tall travel?

answers.text:
Siempre en el asiento delantero, con un dispositivo de retención homologado adaptado a su talla y peso, para mejor control.
Always in the front seat, with an approved restraint device suitable for their size and weight, for better control.

Siempre en los traseros, con un dispositivo de retención homologado adaptado a su talla y peso.
Always in the rear seats, with an approved restraint device suitable for their size and weight.

questions.help:
7 Seat belts
 
7.2 Use
However, minors who are 135 centimetres tall or less must use officially approved child retention systems, properly adapted to their height and weight.
These retention systems must always be installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, as they indicate how they must be used and in which vehicle types to ensure safe travel.
(Página 76 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Seat belts
 
7.2 Use
Vehicles for up to nine occupants including driver
In this type of vehicle, minors who are 135 centimetres tall or less must travel in the back seats and use the pertinent child retention systems.
Minors who are taller than 135 centimetres may travel either in the front or back seats, with officially approved seatbelts that are properly fastened.
However, because the seat belt is designed for adults, for safety it is advisable that they use approved child retention devices adapted to their size and weight.
(Página 76 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
8 Speed limits are a necessity
 
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous factors that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the designated speed of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do otherwise means that safety will be compromised.
(Página 177 del manual 'Learning to drive')
